- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.67) and recent history shows upward momentum.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative (especially <0.33) or shows recent reversal.
- Overshoot after sharp upward spikes in sentiment; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% for 3–5 day horizon.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, adjust downward by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Lagged sentiment: if sentiment drops sharply 2–3 days prior, reduce forecast by 3–5% to account for delayed market reaction.
- Avoid overconfidence in 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed or trending downward; cap forecast at 10% below 14-day moving average if sentiment <0.5.
